channel.title: GUI Agents Papers
channel.description: A curated, searchable list of research papers on GUI agents — models, frameworks, benchmarks, datasets, and more.

item.title: Can LLM Agents Learn to Test? Maintaining Scoped Experience as Testing Evidence for Mobile GUI Testing
item.description: Presents a scoped experience retention mechanism for mobile GUI testing agents, selectively caching valid locators and recovery routines while pruning context that does not generalize across app revisions to improve automated test coverage.

item.title: MKD2World: A Typed Spatial MarkDown World Model For Web Agents
item.description: MKD2World introduces Typed Spatial MarkDown as a structured world model representation for web agents, encoding layout topology and UI semantics to accurately predict post-action interface states for look-ahead agent planning.

item.title: Securing Web Agents with the Compile-Then-Execute Paradigm
item.description: Introduces Baya, a compile-then-execute architecture that compiles high-level web agent workflows into static plans before browsing, isolating control flow from untrusted webpage observations to eliminate indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities.

item.title: Visual Token Routing: Learning to keep tokens that matter
item.description: Visual Token Routing (VTR) trains a lightweight router to dynamically select informative visual tokens from screenshots, matching full-resolution performance on OSWorld and CUA-World with 2.5-5.8x fewer tokens and 3.3x lower inference costs.

item.title: JHiMA-WebRL: A Joint Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Long-Horizon Web Tasks
item.description: JHiMA-WebRL coordinates high-level planning and low-level action execution through joint hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning, optimizing policy collaboration to substantially boost success rates on complex VisualWebArena workflows.

item.title: ScamWorld: An Interactive Environment for Evaluating Web Agents Against Online Fraud
item.description: ScamWorld is an interactive testbed reconstructing documented online fraud schemes (fake stores, investment scams), revealing that frontier web agents fall for deception in 11% to 35% of tasks by proceeding with unauthorized payments and credential entry.

item.title: CUA-Master: Scaling Computer-use Agents through Open-World Recursive Improvements
item.description: CUA-Master scales computer-use agents through open-world recursive improvement, iteratively discovering novel software tasks, generating validated self-training demonstrations, and refining GUI grounding policies across diverse desktop workflows.

item.title: Coati: Host-Grounded Execution for Installable Mobile GUI Agents
item.description: Coati provides host-grounded execution for installable mobile GUI agents running directly on Android devices without requiring external host computers or ADB connections, enforcing strict security and interaction isolation.

item.title: Computer-Use Agents Gain Little Benefit from a World Model When Conditioned on Tutorials
item.description: Investigates the role of world models in computer-use agents, finding that look-ahead simulation provides marginal gains when agents are supplied with task tutorials, and that tutorial grounding alone drives the majority of performance improvements on OSWorld.

item.title: From Local Skills to Long-Horizon Web Tasks: Progressive Skill Exploration for LLM Web Agents
item.description: Proposes a progressive skill exploration framework that bootstraps web agents by acquiring localized atomic navigation skills before composing them into long-horizon trajectories, boosting task completion on WebArena and Mind2Web.

item.title: MAGAR: Multimodal Agents for GUI-Based 3D Mechanical Assembly and Minimal Rework
item.description: MAGAR deploys multimodal GUI agents to operate complex 3D CAD modeling software for mechanical assembly, incorporating geometric constraint verification and backtrack planning to minimize rework during automated CAD modeling.

item.title: ScienceCUA: Resource-to-Skill Construction and Execution-Guided Skill Evolution for Scientific Computer Use Agents
item.description: ScienceCUA transforms software documentation into executable operational skills and queryable references for scientific computer use agents, using execution feedback on ScienceBoard benchmarks to evolve skills and boost task success by up to 17.1%.

item.title: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
item.description: WebHarbor provides 153 executable and dockerized website environments with 3,518 tasks covering complex post-authentication workflows, supporting deterministic evaluation and scalable reinforcement learning for multimodal GUI web agents.

item.title: Interface Quilt: Modifying Applications with Computer Use Agents and Generative UI
item.description: Interface Quilt pairs computer-use agents with generative UI to augment closed-source desktop applications without APIs, synthesizing custom overlays and automating underlying GUI operations directly through vision and action execution.

item.title: NorthCUA Technical Report: Turbocharging Computer-Use Agents through Experience at Scale
item.description: Presents NorthCUA, an integrated computer-use agent system featuring an Experience Flywheel and recursive self-improvement that curates verified execution trajectories at scale, achieving state-of-the-art performance across desktop automation benchmarks.

item.title: MAPLE: A Multimodal Mobile Agent with Playbook-Learned Experience
item.description: MAPLE equips multimodal mobile agents with structured operational playbooks extracted from past experience, enabling reliable task execution across diverse Android apps through dynamic guideline retrieval and self-correction.

item.title: ANGLER: Verifier-Grounded Benchmarking with an Adaptive Attacker for Web Agents
item.description: Introduces REEF, an executable benchmark covering 9 verifier-grounded websites, and ANGLER, an adaptive near-miss guided lure evolution framework that stress-tests web agents against environmental and user-level prompt injection attacks.

item.title: Hybrid Computer Use: A Unified Programmatic, Semantic, and Visual Interface for General Agents
item.description: Proposes Hybrid Computer Use (HCU), unifying programmatic code execution, semantic accessibility tree inspection, and visual GUI interaction into a coordinated interface, outperforming single-modality baselines on OSWorld 2.0.

item.title: MemU-Bench: Benchmarking GUI Agents on Long-Horizon User Interactions
item.description: MemU-Bench evaluates GUI agents on 118 vague, history-dependent tasks grounded in 29 long-horizon interaction streams, benchmarking how well agents recall and distill prior user interactions without relying on brute-force UI searches.

item.title: AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers
item.description: AgentHeal benchmarks web agent error recovery across realistic online access barriers (dead links, auth walls, rate limits), evaluating whether agents can preserve overall goals through alternative workflows.

item.title: DynaRev: Benchmarking Web Agents under Dynamic Goal Revision
item.description: DynaRev benchmarks web agents under dynamic goal revision across 181 tasks spanning multiple websites, evaluating how agents adapt intermediate progress and recover from invalidated actions when requirements change during execution.

item.title: EnvOS: Auditing Computer-Use Agents When the World Moves On : Phenomenon-Based Task Construction, Certification, and Evidence-Based Evaluation
item.description: EnvOS introduces a phenomenon-based auditing framework for computer-use agents, synthesizing certified environment mutations and evidence-based grading to evaluate agent resilience when software states, appointments, and policies change mid-task.

item.title: InterA11y: Interactive Web Accessibility Error Detection with LLM Agents
item.description: InterA11y combines structured WCAG rubrics with deterministic interactive tools to enable LLM agents to detect accessibility issues across dynamic, interactive web states with high precision and recall.

item.title: Mage-VL-Cowork: A Full Training Recipe to Learn Hybrid Computer Use From Evolved Harnesses
item.description: Mage-VL-Cowork presents an end-to-end training recipe for hybrid computer use, combining visual GUI interactions with code execution across midtraining, SFT, and RL to achieve 66.0% success on OSWorld-Verified with a compact 4B model.

item.title: Online Dense Reinforcement Learning with Planning-Grounding Agent for UI Navigation on Live IOS Apps
item.description: Trains decoupled planning and UI grounding agents via online PPO with dense step rewards and neighbor-conditioned value estimation across hundreds of concurrent live iOS devices, outperforming Gemini-3.5-Flash.

item.title: VeriCUA: Verification as Agentic Exploration for Computer-Using Agents
item.description: VeriCUA frames task-completion verification as agentic exploration, deploying an autonomous verification agent that inspects runtime environment states and application side effects, dramatically improving verification precision over passive VLM judges.

item.title: What Does "Now" Mean to Your Computer-Use Agent? Stale Screenshots, Page Loads, and Which Check to Run Before a Click
item.description: Analyzes the risk of stale clicks due to asynchronous page loading in computer-use agents, demonstrating that preflight pixel checks eliminate misclicks with minimal latency overhead compared to full VLM re-planning.

item.title: Where to Learn and How Far to Roll Out: Efficient Adaptive Training for GUI Agents
item.description: Introduces an adaptive two-stage training framework for multi-step GUI agents that selects informative intermediate checkpoints via action disagreement and optimizes rollouts to avoid redundant prefix re-execution.

item.title: AdaGround: Token-Normalized Adaptive Zooming with Verifier-in-the-Loop Refinement for GUI Grounding
item.description: AdaGround addresses high-resolution screen grounding failures via token-normalized adaptive zooming and an interactive verifier-in-the-loop that re-evaluates ambiguous targets.

item.title: From Interaction to Capability: Task Advancement as State and Supervision for GUI Agents
item.description: Introduces Task Advancement Memory (TAM), defining task progress states as dense supervision to help GUI agents retain valuable operation milestones and avoid cascading errors in cross-application workflows.

item.title: GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latents as a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents
item.description: GUI-JEPA replaces slow autoregressive token decoding with candidate-conditioned Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) latents, speeding up mobile GUI action selection by up to 8x.

item.title: Learning to Look Beyond Screens: Transferable Visual Observation from GUI Grounding
item.description: LBS leverages GUI grounding trajectories as spatial supervision to train vision-language models for active visual perception and multi-turn crop-and-inspect exploration that transfers beyond screens to complex multimodal benchmarks.

item.title: Right Click, Wrong Box: Grading GUI Grounding by What a Click Does
item.description: Demonstrates that bounding-box overlap metrics misjudge GUI grounding performance, proposing an outcome-grounded grading metric that assesses whether a predicted click actually triggers the intended UI behavior.

item.title: WebAnything: From the Wild Web to Scalable Agent Environments
item.description: WebAnything automatically reconstructs source-grounded, executable, and resettable web environments directly from live URLs via an Explorer-Builder loop and independent verification without per-site engineering.

item.title: Back to Basics: A Skill-Centric Approach to Generalist Web Agents
item.description: Introduces MiniWeb, a 65-site benchmark that labels tasks by 37 interaction skills, and MiniWebGen, which generates verified skill-focused training data, then pairs a skill-trained 4B model with a task-decomposing planner to improve task success by 19.4 points on unseen sites and 9 to 20 points on WebArena-Lite, Online-Mind2Web, and WebVoyager.

item.title: Chart the Invisible: Interactive Perception for Hidden-Target Exploration in GUI Agents
item.description: Presents Hagasu, a multimodal model for scrollable-region perception that helps mobile GUI agents detect hidden elements and execute targeted swipe exploration, boosting task completion from 64.8% to 82.7%.

item.title: GUIFlow: Temporal Redundancy-Aware Incremental Inference for GUI Agents
item.description: GUIFlow exploits temporal redundancy across successive GUI screenshots, using localized bounding-box delta encoding and token reuse to accelerate multi-step VLM inference by over 2.5x without accuracy loss.

item.title: SkillLifeBench: Benchmarking Security Across the Lifecycle of Agent Skills
item.description: SkillLifeBench benchmarks security across the lifecycle of agent skills in web environments, assessing vulnerability to malicious skill reconfiguration, execution divergence, and provenance spoofing across 388 scenarios.

item.title: iPrefBench: A User-Centric Benchmark for Personalized Mobile Use Agents
item.description: iPrefBench evaluates infer-and-ask capabilities of personalized mobile agents in an executable iOS environment across 26 apps and 130 underspecified tasks, revealing that current frontier models struggle with ask-only requirements.

item.title: AgentProofBench: Benchmarking Reusable Verifiers for Web Agents
item.description: AgentProofBench benchmarks reusable verifiers for web agents, evaluating whether programmatic acceptance checks can verify variable business states without suffering from state leakage or false acceptance.

item.title: AndroidFlux: Evaluating Failure Recovery and Recovery Action Reward Modeling in Mobile-Use Multimodal Agents
item.description: AndroidFlux benchmarks failure recovery across 247 Android tasks and trains a recovery action reward model that significantly enhances mobile agent resilience on AndroidWorld.

item.title: Build or Adopt? Custom-Built vs. General-Purpose LLM Agent Harnesses for Automotive GUI Testing
item.description: Empirically compares a custom production agent harness against general-purpose agent harnesses for Android-based automotive in-vehicle infotainment (IVI) GUI testing at Volvo Group.

item.title: OS-Wizard: Scaling Computer-Using Agents to Specialized Software via Knowledge-Guided Exploration
item.description: OS-Wizard combines tutorial-guided exploration with a hybrid GUI-Code action space to automate high-quality trajectory collection for specialized desktop software like CAD and GIS tools.

item.title: PreView: Enhancing GUI Grounding with Preprocessed Views and Cues
item.description: PreView is an auxiliary preprocessor that improves inputs to frozen grounding models via localized visual crops and contextual cues, boosting grounding accuracy on small and dense controls without retraining.

item.title: Seeing the Options: Typed Decisions over Visual Candidates with Reusable Option Memory
item.description: Introduces Iris, an architecture for typed decisions over visual candidates (e.g. element screenshot crops on Multimodal-Mind2Web) that guarantees candidate order-invariance and cuts latency up to 191x via reusable option memory.

item.title: SkillShift-Bench: Benchmarking Skill Learning under Environment Evolution for Web Agents
item.description: SkillShift-Bench evaluates whether learned web agent skills remain effective as websites undergo interface redesigns, DOM restructuring, and workflow changes over time.

item.title: Correct Answers, Closed Gates: SolveBind for GUI Agents at the Verification Barrier
item.description: SolveBind bridges solver reasoning with behavioral verification in protected GUI environments, generating human-like interaction trajectories to satisfy anti-automation defense mechanisms.

item.title: IGG: A Benchmark for Interactive GUI Grounding under Visibility Constraints
item.description: IGG benchmarks interactive GUI grounding under partial visibility, requiring agents to actively explore, scroll, and reveal non-visible controls rather than assuming all elements are on screen.

item.title: Diagnosing Personalization Failures in Mobile GUI Agents
item.description: Analyzes how and when user preferences should alter execution in personalized mobile GUI agents, categorizing personalization failure modes and proposing structured preference mediation.

item.title: Learning What to Ask for Tomorrow: Active Preference Acquisition for Long-Term Personalized Web Agents
item.description: Studies active preference acquisition for web agents serving the same user across repeated tasks, formulating prospective personalization value to decide which missing preferences are worth asking about.

item.title: PointerBench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Fine-Grained GUI Grounding
item.description: PointerBench is a diagnostic benchmark of 1,500 pairs probing thin sub-element identification in spreadsheets, character-level text grounding, and complex controls across 100 professional desktop applications.

item.title: Reuse, Rewrite, or Reject: Evidence-Constrained Trace Reuse for Repeated Mobile GUI Control
item.description: Presents an evidence-constrained trace reuse framework that validates past mobile GUI execution steps against current context, reusing valid transitions, rewriting invalidated ones, and rejecting infeasible steps.

item.title: Subgoal-aware Memory Graph for GUI Agent
item.description: Proposes a subgoal-aware memory graph that distills past trajectories into structured, reusable evidence at the subgoal level to guide mobile GUI agents through complex, long-horizon tasks.

item.title: Trace2World: Reconstructing App Worlds from Real Interaction Traces for Scalable GUI Agent Training
item.description: Trace2World reconstructs source-linked executable mock environments from real interaction traces for scalable GUI agent reinforcement learning without manual implementation.

item.title: Who Verifies the Agent's Success Claim? Self-Report Leakage in GUI-Agent Completion Judging
item.description: Investigates dangerous misreports where GUI agents falsely report success, identifying self-report leakage in completion judging and proposing independent verification to safeguard automation pipelines.

item.title: CUA-Recovery: Benchmarking Error Recovery in Long-Horizon Computer-Use Agents
item.description: CUA-Recovery benchmarks error awareness and recovery across desktop workflows using 2,250 verified error states and 8.6K synthesized training trajectories, showing substantial recovery gains after fine-tuning.

item.title: Evolving Agent Interfaces
item.description: Introduces Agent S4, an autonomous computer-use scientist that iteratively evolves agent interfaces and usage knowledge from experience, achieving state-of-the-art open-source performance (21.3%) on OSWorld V2.

item.title: Lost in Recovery: Demystifying Recovery Behavior of Computer-Use Agents via Goal-Oriented Action Replay
item.description: ReTrace evaluates computer-use agent recovery through goal-oriented action replay under controlled error injection, operationalizing transition-consistent recovery to analyze autonomous error mitigation.

item.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
item.description: Proposes WildAWM, an agent world model framework that synthesizes interactive computer-use environments and validates task state transitions, providing scalable and secure training environments for computer-use agents.

item.title: CUA-Lite: An Open Platform for Computer Use Agents
item.description: Presents CUA-Lite, an open platform standardizing computer-use agent development with a unified environment interface across 12 benchmarks, lightweight sandboxes with over 30,000 verifiable tasks, and shared model harnesses for evaluation, RL, and SFT.
